title: A Review of SSSC and Carbon Market Synergies in Wind Energy Integration
content: The integration of wind energy into power systems is vital for global decarbonization goals but faces technical and economic challenges, including transmission losses, grid instability, and risks of disconnection during severe contingencies. This review proposes a synergistic framework that aligns Static Synchronous Series Compensator (SSSC) technology, Security-Constrained Optimal Power Flow (CSCOPF) strategies, and carbon trading mechanisms to enable coordinated benefits for power system stakeholders. SSSC reduces transmission losses, thereby improving the overall transmission efficiency for general power producers and wind energy operators, enabling a more efficient energy flow that contributes to carbon reduction. Part of the resulting carbon credits can be allocated as incentives to transmission operators, creating a mutually beneficial outcome. Simultaneously, CSCOPF ensures grid stability under severe fault conditions, preventing wind farms from disconnection and enabling their continued participation in the carbon trading market, safeguarding both economic returns and decarbonization objectives. By synthesizing existing research, this review highlights the interlocking relationships among technologies, market incentives, and carbon reduction, providing a pathway to achieve sustainable, stable, and economically efficient power systems.
